title: Forty thousand deletions by one merge patch from a mapping of one and a half million keys must stay linear
notes: The input is a block mapping of 1,500,000 keys, `k0000000: value` to `k1499999: value`, 24 megabytes. One RFC 7396 merge patch deletes 39,990 of them with `"kN": null` members (section 2: a null member removes the key). The deleted keys come in thirty runs of 1,333, starting at `k0001000` and then every 49,999 keys, so the deletions are spread over the whole mapping and a library cannot finish by touching one place. (Thirty runs, not 39,990 separate keys, because the expected result is built from a recipe of at most 64 parts: the kept keys in thirty-one runs.) Every other line stays as it was, and a removed entry takes only its own line (there are no comments here, so no convention is involved). The result is the same 24 megabytes without those 39,990 lines, which is far larger than a stored file may be, so the exact bytes come from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md). The patch is valid and its result is small enough that no limit applies to it, so the exact result is the expected answer; a limit error is also accepted, because a library may bound the work or the output of a patch, and then the document must be reported unchanged (a patch is atomic). A library whose cost for each deletion grows with the size of the document (one that reads or indexes the whole document again for every deleted key) does that work 39,990 times over 24 megabytes, 960 billion bytes read, which is the cost this case was built for; moving the rest of the bytes once per deletion is cheap at this size and is not what it is about. The time limit is 100 seconds and is a hang guard, not a measure of cost. The size is chosen so that the guard still has force: a model reader that does nothing but walk the document once per deletion, at 5 GB/s, needs 190 seconds, and a reader that parses or indexes it is slower than that, while libraries that handle each deletion in time proportional to the deletion needed between 1 and 1.5 seconds (measured from the moment the request is written to the last byte of the answer, not a bound). The memory bound is 2048 MB, as in the ten-megabyte sibling, whose accepted answer is also a structure of about a million nodes held in memory: this input has three million scalar nodes (the keys and the values) and the result is held as well, which leaves about 680 bytes for each scalar. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input and the expected result are generated from the recipes in case.json; the case carries the tag `slow` because both are larger than a stored file.

provenance.reference: A patch engine whose merge-patch deletions skipped its work bound, so each of three thousand deletions from a large mapping processed the whole document again and the patch took quadratic time.
